findings.title: Busy/booked time check is skipped entirely for days with a date override
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once a date override is detected for the slot's day and the slot falls inside the override's time window, the function returns `true` immediately (`if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`) before ever reaching the `return busy.every(...)` check at the bottom of the function. This means that for any day on which a host has a date override, existing bookings/busy times for that host on that day are no longer checked at all when determining slot availability. Previously (before this PR) `checkIfIsAvailable` always ran the busy-time check unconditionally. Now, on override days, a user can be shown as available and double-booked into a slot that is already occupied by an existing booking, because the override branch short-circuits before the busy check runs. This directly undermines the booking integrity this function exists to enforce.

findings.title: dayjs instances compared by reference (always false) when detecting all-day/zero-duration overrides
findings.body: The check `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two freshly created dayjs objects with `===`. Since dayjs instances are objects, this reference comparison will always evaluate to false even when the two represent the same instant (e.g. a zero-duration override meant to mark the entire day unavailable). As a result, the intended 'whole day blocked' override case never triggers this branch, and such overrides are silently treated as a regular time range or ignored, which can show slots as available when the organizer explicitly blocked the day. This should use `.isSame()` instead of `===`.

findings.title: Working-hours end check uses slot start time twice instead of slot end time
findings.body: In the new working-hours validation inside checkIfIsAvailable, both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), so the comparison `end > workingHour.endTime` never accounts for how long the slot actually runs (eventLength). A slot that starts within working hours but whose end (slotEndTime) extends past the working-hours end time will incorrectly pass this check and be considered available, allowing bookings that run past the end of the organizer's working hours.

findings.title: override.timeZone is optional but used unguarded for offset calculation
findings.body: `TimeRange.timeZone` (packages/types/schedule.d.ts) was added as an optional field, yet getSlots unconditionally does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. If any caller of getSlots builds dateOverrides without populating `timeZone` (the field is optional and not enforced anywhere in the type system), `.tz(undefined)` will fall back to ambiguous/system-default behavior, producing an incorrect offset and therefore an incorrect override time window silently, rather than failing loudly or falling back to a sane default (e.g. the schedule's own timeZone).

findings.title: No test covers the primary fix: fixed-host date overrides for round-robin events
findings.body: The PR description states its main fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now respected for round-robin event types (so round-robin events aren't bookable when a fixed host is unavailable due to an override). However, the only test added in this PR covers date-override timezone conversion for a single-user personal event; there is no round-robin + fixed-host + date-override scenario test. This leaves the headline bug fix of the PR without automated regression coverage.

findings.title: No test exercises date overrides together with existing busy/booked time
findings.body: The 'Check for Date overrides' test only verifies slot generation against working hours/override boundaries with no bookings present. There is no test combining a date override day with an existing booking (busy time) on that same day, which is exactly the scenario affected by the checkIfIsAvailable early-return bug (dateOverrideExist causing the busy-time check to be skipped). Such a test would have caught the double-booking risk introduced by this change.
